lines.text: I used to make beats. Yeah, cool. Thank you. That's DVDASA — welcome to the show. I'm David Choe, and I'm here with my special guest today, Steve Lee. And we got Val up in here. The show was supposed to start at two today, so thank you for being early. No problem, glad to be here.
You were the first one here. And also — first time here without your brother. And we got Money Mark here playing the beats.
Everyone else is late, but that's fine, because I just want to talk to you anyways. Okay.

What's up, Val? How's it going? Good. Oh, Bobby. What's up, Bob? So there's something very endearing — every time you do the show with your brother, you can tell how much he loves you. Yeah, I know. I love him a lot too, but I don't show it as well as...
[content removed]

...the next comedian, Steven Lee. And I just ran up there, right? And so this lady's sitting about as far as this table — well, not that close, but the closest where I could see her. And I noticed... Does that stall you when you look up and there's someone shaking their head, giving you a stink eye?

Yeah, it kind of fucks with my head, because I'm doing my bit. Were people booing and saying shit? No, it wasn't booing. It's even worse when it's silent. Silence. Yeah. I mean, if I got booed I'd at least get some kind of reaction.

But normally, like when I did that bit at the Meltdown comic book store, it was an applause break. But I realized that bit is for — these people are just older people. They want you to tell regular jokes. Don't do this weird rapping cowboy thing, you know.
So it was quiet. It was kind of quiet. I mean, I heard little glimpses of laughter. Oh, that was probably your brother. Yeah, it was probably Bob.
Yeah, it's brutal. It was brutal. Dude, they cut me from the second show. So you go up like, I'm going to express myself — he lied about it, too — I'm going to express myself through humor on stage.
And you have your routine. You're like, I want to do a good job. And you fail. Yeah, it was a fail. Does it make you never want to do that again?

Where do you find the strength to go on a stage again after a bomb like that? First of all, I know comedians love it when other comedians bomb. I mean, not Bobby. Yeah, it's highly psychological, and I'm learning that too.
Even in the open mic world, people will say stuff. It's like a battle — it's combative. They steal jokes. They try to nitpick. There's a happiness when you fail.

[mock voice] Dude, you should say it this way. That's not funny, dude. They're not killing it — they're an open mic-er, you know what I mean? But yeah, it was very painful. It's kind of like the wrestling thing: what am I going to do? I gotta get back on the horse.

I mean, it's early on in the game. Well, that's what I'm saying — you did give up at the wrestling thing eventually. I know, but that's what I'm saying, I can't make the same mistake. You learned. Yeah, I learned. So I went back on stage.

I did mics at home here, and I went right back out. That wrestling thing's on the back burner, and I'm just trying to write more general stuff. In my limited exposure to professional comedians, what I've seen is it's such a brutal thing to go on stage.

Like, what I do is art, and if someone came to an art show and started talking shit about my paintings — well, they do that, I'm sure. Yeah, it happens all the time. But first of all, I've developed a thicker skin, and two, I don't even have to go to the art show.

You don't have to interact with them. Even if it's your show, you don't have to interact with them. And it's not like I'm physically standing there saying, judge me. Judge what I'm saying. It's so weird. So what I've seen from comedians who travel the road, on the circuit, touring or whatever—

Your brother's brilliant at that. I've seen him switch with the audience. That's great advice. He'll have a fucking hick town and do hick jokes, and then he'll have a hipster crowd and do jokes that wouldn't go through in the hick town.

He plays to the audience. Oh yeah, he could be smoking a cigarette — oh, you're up next — and he'll just go, boom. He's a real professional. He's a professional. But the problem with comedians and hard drugs and addiction and things like that — [someone walks in] hi, how's it going? Awesome — is, say you're in fucking buttfuck Tennessee and you bombed like that. Yeah, dude.
I could see the appeal of wanting to go to your hotel room, where there's no drummer or bass player, where you're like, hey, we suck tonight. No — it's just you. You suck tonight.
You bombed. Let's do some heroin. Let's get into some drugs or alcohol or whatever. That's why there's a lot of abuse going on — because of that pain, to deal with it.
But you and your brother are addicts — ex-addicts, recovering addicts. But I don't use anymore. But when you go on stage and you bomb like that — I have to feel the pain. You just feel it.
I feel it. I feel every bit of it. There's no coding it. There's nothing in you that makes you want to do drugs again? Well, I can't lie — a beer would be nice. But I don't want to do that.
I have five years of sobriety. I don't want to ruin my recovery just for one bad incident. Did you do drugs, or was it just alcohol?

Mostly weed and beer, but I dabbled in hallucinogenics. What's up, Pooner? Why don't you sit over here with your new buddy, Steve? Yeah, just mostly beer and weed. Whose fault is it that you guys are late? Whoa, I was trying — but it's never Bill, just so you know. Every time we've—
[content removed]

Welcome one, welcome all. It's DVDASA with your hosts, David Choe and Asa Akira. We have a very special guest, Steve Lee, here. We got Bill Poon, Valentin with his great stories, Critter, and last but not least, Money Mark on the keys.
Here we go. Here we go. It'll be trivia, yo. Thanks, Critter. Where's your brother? I don't know. Buying oil? Yeah, he had something — a meeting, or I don't know.

Buying more oil. He's always — sometimes the show will end and he'll have to go right away, and we'll say, hey, Steve, you hang out, and he'll be like, no, Steve's coming with me. He's always sheltering him. He's very selfish with you. I think it's more controlling than—
Protective. Yeah, it's more controlling. So he let you come today without him? Yeah, and I'm happy to be here. I feel freer. Wait, he let you come?

Well, whatever, you know what I'm saying. He didn't cock-block. He didn't go, you can only go when I go. Well, cool. Look, the Lee brothers are hilarious. We think you're the funnier brother. Don't ever say that, though. She just said it. And I back it up. We said it like ten times last night.

In the comedian world, it's the contrary. Steve, listen — your brother is hilarious. He's the funniest comedian, he kills, he's the funniest of all Asian comedians, he's a professional. But you're just funny. Like, you don't have to tell jokes. If you went like this, it would be funny. I wish it could translate into—

I know what you're saying, and I think it will. Your brother — as he practiced, he got better, and you'll get better too. But you gotta stick with it. So when you bombed in Tucson, in Tempe, and you get to this point where you're sad, you just jump back on the horse. That's great.
[content removed]

So you're playing video games all night. FIFA — I'm doing FIFA 14. I'm doing the Korean league. What time do you go to sleep? I'm weird, I'm vampire style. So I'm either doing that, or — I have a short memory span, so I'll do that for like two hours.

Or three hours. Sometimes I lose track of time. You're committed to the FIFA. Video games are great. Did that replace the drugs? I think so. It's probably the number one addiction. What are you doing — FIFA in career mode?
What does that mean when you say you do FIFA in career mode? Well, in career mode, you assemble your own team and send out scouts to different countries to scout out players. It's like a fantasy.

You're like, oh, I'm really finding this young talent, and you groom them, and then you watch them improving their stats. Sounds like an unbelievable investment of time. I know, it's more of a fantasy.
Tony does it too, and he's totally addicted. He's addicted to the point where he's asked me to learn how to do it, so that when he's not home, I can train the players.

So the training is happening. And I'm like, no. Wow, that's awesome. Is the training happening in real time? No, you're just finding him — it's just the name of the guy. But you're taking a lot of time.

I'm going to every country. I'm going to, like, Nigeria. First class? You're flying first class? Well, you could, depending on how many months you want to send out your scout. Do you know all the technical rules and regulations, everything about soccer — before, or just through this game?
I think I've learned a lot. Both of us — even Bob — got into soccer through FIFA. We never even watched it. We bought the 2006 one and we played that.
You love it. Yeah, and then we're like, oh, Beckham. Who wins? It's actually 50-50. We both play the same — he knows what I'm gonna do every time, how I'm gonna cut and stuff like that.

But he's a genius. In his defense, my brother's a genius with video games. If he wasn't a comedian, he could probably be a gamer. Wait a minute — if he's a genius at video games and he only beats you 50-50—
—that means you're a genius. No, no, no. That's just FIFA. There are other video games — when he plays Fallout or Skyrim, the guy's a genius. You're too modest.
You're modest. Remember when the new GTA came out? Like a week later, he was talking about how he'd already completed it. Yeah, he probably gets into it the same way he used to do drugs.

Big time. Right? When he lived above the Comedy Store — I think it was Oblivion, Elder Scrolls — he closed the drapes and just had his cigarettes and Red Bull. How deep is it? He was deep into it. But how deep is it between you and your brother? Like—

It comes before, like, girls? You'd pick video games over women? Well, that's a touchy subject. I don't want him to get mad at me. Oh, he's not gonna listen to this shit. I don't give a fuck. Yeah, that's true. It might have kind of intervened—

You know how much shit I talk about your brother when he's on here? He's never gonna hear it. Well, it may have affected — especially the Fallouts and the Skyrims, the kinds of games he likes. Steve, I'm only asking because I know what they do to me.

I don't even take the plastic off. I buy them so it gives me some comfort, knowing that if I need to go into that dark place, I own it, I possess it. But I know what happens the day I open it. Like, Mark works with—
—the Rockstar guys, and they sent me a huge package with all the Grand Theft shit and all this paraphernalia. Yeah, Bob played that two or three times. I think he's on his third time now.
He'll beat a game, then create a different character and play the whole game from the beginning. Dude, I'm there. So, going back—
I'll play a game like Grand Theft Auto and pass the game, and then I'll just be a character and walk through the game. I'll just walk — not even steal a car, just get in a car.
Just enjoy it, and just drive. And I want to do it in a room with all the curtains drawn. I don't want someone to come in and judge.
[mock voice] What are you doing? Oh, you're driving a car, or going for a walk on the beach? They're like, you know you could actually just leave and go for a walk on the beach?

I'm like, no, I want to walk on the beach in the fucking video game, you know? And that's what Bob likes — the role-playing games. There are first-person shooters, but he likes the freedom of just exploring. He'll walk up a mountain and be like, oh, I found this cave and I walked in there.
And he explores the world. Look, it's one of the biggest addictions facing our country today. It's a rich, rich source for comedy. I know. Why don't you mine some of this?
We were talking about it in the other room, and I didn't think about it, but I might even tap into that, because you don't see a lot of bits on it.

Why would you say 'mine'? Why don't you do it? Well, I'm going to try to write bits. I don't know anything about FIFA, and I hate soccer. When you start talking about career mode, I don't even know what you're talking about — and you could talk about it forever.
It's only going to get bigger — the Xbox One just dropped, the new consoles are dropping. Do you have any interest in real soccer? I love watching real soccer. But because of FIFA.

Because of FIFA. But I enjoy the game now, because it was the catalyst to get me into that world. So you know all the players now. Oh yeah, we're Arsenal fans. Who's doing good right now in the world?

In the Premier League, Arsenal — we're leading, we're number one right now, but Theo Walcott just got hurt. So how's Korea doing? Korea? No, I'm talking about in reality — do you know what's going on in real-life soccer?
Yeah, we watch the game, we watch the Premier League. If I sent you as a representative for DVDASA — like a reporter to cover the World Cup — would you go?
Dude, are you kidding me? I don't know. I'm all the way there. You wouldn't sleep till four? For the World Cup? Dude, that'd be crazy. It's in Brazil, right?
I can't even — I'm trying to think about the man-hours it takes to create a game like FIFA. If you're able to fly to countries and scout players, it sounds like — whatever.
There are so many players in that game that some of them don't even have a picture. If they're young or don't have a lot of stats, they'll just have a blank icon, a blank profile.

Right, just a silhouette. Earlier last year, me and Critter went to Afghanistan with Estevan Oriol. And our host in Afghanistan owns the soccer league there. And he asked me if I wanted to buy an Afghani soccer team for a million or two million.
A million, yeah. A million. That's all it costs? It's an Afghani soccer team. Are they even in the world? I don't think they're even supposed to play. They barely qualified or whatever.

I don't think they're going to the World Cup. Wait, hold on — the World Cup is only two teams, right? No, all the countries that qualify. You have to qualify. So they don't qualify. I'm sure Afghanistan — I don't want to be negative, but I'm pretty sure they didn't qualify. I don't know.

Loser talk. Are all the players Afghani? I mean, if I bought the team, I'd bring in Beckham and stuff. Yeah, you can scout out — I'm sure Beckham is so expensive. Well, I'm not talking about David Beckham.

I'm talking about Raul Beckham. David Beckham? Yeah, it's his weird cousin. They do that in Hollywood sometimes. I think in the '90s there was a movie with Stallone, Schwarzenegger, and Swayze — and it was all their brothers.

It was some weird movie. So how confident are you? I never even thought about it — the offer was made and I was like, that would be funny if I owned an Afghani soccer team. If I bought the Afghani soccer team, do you think you could go coach the team?

I know nothing about that. Are you prepared to live in Kabul, and do drills like suicide-bomber tests with them? I know nothing about — but you're a good scouter, right? It's a video game. But they're real players, though, right?
Because these are real people you're talking about. This is a video game, compared to real life. But aren't they based on the real people? I don't even know. I didn't even know they had a league.
Steve, let's talk about your future for a second, okay? You're sitting next to a wise old Asian guy that's about ten, twelve years older than you. You're forty years old right now.
Thirty-nine. Thirty-nine, okay. Oh, we gotta do a big party for you. When's your birthday, Steve? August 25th. Okay, we're gonna do a big party for you.

Cool. Or — you're buying the doll. No, you don't have to get the doll. You're forty years old. In ten years, when you're fifty, do you see yourself running an Afghani soccer team in Kabul? Or do you see yourself getting to Bobby's level in comedy? Where do you see yourself at fifty?

Family, kids running around? The whole Afghani-soccer-coach thing is so crazy that it just might work. I know nothing about it — you have to understand, I don't know anything about it. I watch it, I'm a fan of it. You can't sit here and say you don't know. What do you do in career mode?

But that's a video game. What do you do in career mode? Okay, you play the games, but you scout out — you can send scouts out to different countries, but you don't do the work. The video-game world does that. So you just send them to, like, Nigeria, and you go—
What are you looking for? I'm looking for a winger, or a technically gifted player. And then they just — listen to me — you get a report back and then you see — why can't you do that in real life?
Because it's different. I believe in you. I don't know any of the Afghan players. I'm going to make a million-dollar investment into this team. I'll pay — you don't have to do that.

Listen. I'm going to design their uniforms. I'm going to get Prada or someone to make them. It's going to be the sickest uniforms ever. You need to train these fuckers. You need to put bombs on their chests and make them do running drills.

And if they fail, they're off the team, because they're dead. And then you're gonna work these fuckers. [deadpan] I think that's called murder. And this is gonna be like Snow Dogs — no, no, Cool Runnings. And you're gonna get this team, and in ten years they might qualify. Who's the best in the World Cup, Val?
It's like Mexico, Spain, Germany, Brazil. Brazil, Spain. When people talk about the World Cup now, it'll be Afghanistan, Spain, Germany. Can you do that? Is that too much of a challenge for you?
I mean, it's so crazy, it just might work. You should be jumping on this. I would. Do you know what the quality of life in Kabul is? No, I don't even know anything about it.
It's horrible. So where would I be staying? No, you'd stay there, but your entire life would change. I would be there. Your quality of life— Why couldn't he do it from here?

He's the coach — he's gotta be there. But can't the team just practice here? No. Or does it not work like that? Does the team have to live in the country? Actually, I don't know. I don't know anything about soccer. Is there a basket or something?
No, no, no. When they're training, to go to another city — can you use your elbows in soccer? Yeah. No — can you touch the ball with your elbow?

No, you can't. You can't touch it with your hands, but you can touch it with your head. Yeah. Steve, I'm putting my hand up and letting you know: I know nothing about soccer, okay? The only thing I know about soccer is that sometimes the Koreans would get to the park, and there'd be Mexicans, and it would always be Korea versus Mexico. That's the only thing I know — and that everyone in the world loves soccer, but they call it football, besides Americans. People go crazy. So they want you to buy their team. This was an offer that was made to me a year ago. There's gonna be a team in the league, yeah.

What's the league called again? I think it's the Saudi — what's the league called in Afghanistan? Emirates? No, Emirates is — FIFA sanctions it. It's not even a real FIFA team. They just barely got sanctioned. It's a farm team. Do you know the players — anyone?
Abdul. Name what? But if you buy the thing, I think you're going to have to spend more money. Yeah. You'll have to buy players. It's not going to be a million dollars.
I'm Korean. I'm not buying it for a million. I'll get it for like — 500,000. I'll get it for 350. You might have to fix the stadium. And what's his salary going to be?
That's their first offer to me. Yeah, does Steve have a salary? He's gotta get his salary. I would know what players do — I know which players are good in the game and in real life.
No, we're going to recreate all these people as if it's a video game. We're going to take them, give them special haircuts, tattoo certain faces, change their name to like Osama. Do you understand?

[dead serious] It's not serious. My whole life, Steve, is a fucking shit show. My whole life is taking something that's retardedly stupid and so crazy that it just might work, and taking it seriously. I'm as serious as you're serious. If you're serious, then I'm serious. If you're not serious, then forget it, you know?
So I don't know — if you have faith in me to scout out players. Do you believe in yourself? I do. I mean, I'm just being honest with you. I play FIFA.
I love Arsenal. I like the players that I like. The way to make this work — you're a sports guy. How would we make this work? They're mostly Afghani guys, but then we bring in a couple, like—
Yeah, you're probably allowed a few. Okay, so we— No, you're definitely allowed a bunch. You gotta pay for this, you gotta buy them. Could your whole team be not—

No, you gotta scout, you gotta bring other players in. No, but I'm saying, does the Afghani team have to have a certain percentage of Afghani players? The uniforms are gonna be dynamite — with ticking time bombs.
[content removed]

...that worked. There was just, like, running and bringing us pitas or whatever. And what was he on? The national bike-riding team — like bike racing. Of Afghanistan? Yeah. And the guy we were with is like, if you sponsor their team, get them some jerseys and some nice bikes—
They don't have jerseys? I mean, I'm sure they have jerseys. I don't know. They get shot at. They don't got anything. They have nothing. So I'm like, if I sent them a package of some—

It's a true Cool Runnings story. But there are athletes out there — dudes ready to go. Oh yeah. They play anywhere. They like playing. The reason soccer is huge all over the world is because all you need is a ball.
That's it. That's all you need. I mean, if we're talking about professional football, though. And you'd have to come in confident. You couldn't come in going, I don't know what I'm doing, guys.
[content removed]
...someone like that. I don't know what you said, but yeah. You know what you're talking about. Well, from — I like watching it, I'm a fan of soccer, but I've never coached.
I played when I was a kid. Coach them the same way you played them in the video game. So just treat it like a video game? Treat it exactly like a video game.
Okay, then if you want me to do that, I think I could do that. Do you want to do that? I mean, yeah, that's a dream. Bobby, buy the team. Bobby, call Saad and tell him we're going to buy the team.
[content removed]
I would have to think about it a little bit. Like, what percent are you in? 50-50. That's it? Wow. Because that's kind of a different life, you know what I mean?

Steve, how long have you been addicted to FIFA? Since 2006. Wow, so you're deep into it. I play it almost every day. How much? I don't compete — I've never done anything that long. Usually it's just me battling Bob back and forth. Do you play online?

No, we just play each other. And in career mode, do you save it? No, that's different. When we're not playing, when I'm just doing my own thing, I do career mode. It's like my own little getaway. So is there a profile?
That you save and start again? Yeah, I have mine. What would happen to you if I deleted that? I'll just create a new career. But isn't there an investment of a tremendous amount of time?
Yeah, because I'm in my fifth season. So would you go into the red zone? No, I wouldn't. I'd be a little upset. I'd be like, oh God, why'd you do that?

But I would just make another career mode. What's the name of your team? I'm managing Arsenal right now. Val, do you think you could coach a soccer team? No. He'd be better suited. You play soccer, right?

No. Like, for fun, though. But he knows about it. But not anymore. You stopped? Yeah. Why? I don't play anymore. Why? Because I have a surgeon in my leg. Oh shit, your leg hurts. Yeah, I couldn't run. But do you think—
If Steve was head coach and you were assistant coach — yeah, we can do that. See if he can. That'd be, you know. But do you want to live in Afghanistan?
[content removed]

Is he a good dude? He's the best dude. And we could take one trip out there just to check it out, and you could decide then. You're not going to be able to skateboard ever again. Oh no, there's no sidewalks. There's no sidewalks. It's like cobblestone. Yeah, it's like just dirt.

There's no street. There are streets — sewer roads, down the gutter. I mean, well, if you own the team, you could just build a skate park. Yeah, and you could bring skateboarding to Afghanistan. There's that skateboard team from Afghanistan. Yeah, there's a skate team in Afghanistan. But there's nowhere for them to skate.
So you wanna go? Let's go. It's either that, or just keep playing the video game. I mean, this is a dream. This is a dream. Is it a dream, or is it a nightmare?
I'm telling you, it's not really a dream. I guess it depends on how you look at it. I think it could be a dream. I mean, what if they end up being good, for a freak cause?
It's so crazy, it just might work. They get a job in the U.S. coaching. Do they even exist in the video game? I don't even know if the league's in FIFA. This is the first time I'm hearing about—
I didn't know about — I wasn't familiar with the league. So how crazy would that be? A team that people don't even know. It's only in Israel. Only Israel? Yeah, the players are only there.

How does Israel do? They have a good player called Yossi Benayoun. There's a good midfield player. Who are the worst teams in FIFA? Well, the Asian League's pretty weak. Really? I thought Japan and South Korea were good.
Yeah, I thought Korea. I don't think — the Saudi Pro League, I think there's a Saudi Pro League that's not that great. Yeah, but it's better than the other ones. Hey, didn't you eat lunch already?
I had brunch. Do you have brunch, or 'brunch'? It wasn't brunch. You know what brunch is? Lunch with just your bros — no girls. [proudly] It's the masculine brunch. No, but there were no girls there.

Here, talk close to your mic. It's — I'm just trying to stay away. No, stay close. I want to talk to you. That sandwich looks delicious. Yeah, where'd you get that sandwich? It's overflowing with mayo.

Roman's Pizza? You know he gets extra. Yeah, where did you get that sandwich — Roman's Pizza? What is that, a ham sandwich? Looks really good. Talk closer to the mic. So I say to you, hey, you want to get lunch, and you say, I already ate lunch, and then you show up with a sandwich.

No — so did you lie to me? Like, someone didn't want to brunch. Yeah, you didn't want to brunch with me. No, I had brunch, and then you called me right after — like an hour after you had brunch with Quiet C. So, okay — the time I texted you is right now, two hours ago. So you got hungry.

After brunch — yeah, it's just about the right time, around two. What did you have for brunch? I had egg in a hole. Nice, that's pretty good. Okay, so you ate that, I texted you, I said, hey, you want to get lunch, you said, I just ate, and then within that hour you got hungry again, like two—

—hours after that. I had to pick up my dry cleaning. Are you lying to me right now? No, I had to pick up my dry cleaning, and I had to pick up Val. So then I'm like, let's go, we're gonna wait for the dry cleaning, so we might as well get food. So you and Val went together? Yeah. Did you eat a—
—sandwich? No, it's their own brunch. Yeah, he's a professional, he lets it get cold. Did you get the sandwich because you were hungry, or just to fill up time? A little of both.
No, but we're going to have a long day today. Pass that sandwich over, I want a bite. It's pretty killer. No, don't take it. I want a bite. I want a bite of the sandwich.
He offered a bite. He offered a bite. He also wants a bite. I don't want it. What is this? Do you go here specifically? It's a pizza place that you go to for the sandwiches?
They have everything. They call it Roman's Pizza, but they have pasta, Mexican food. Oh, that's good, there are pickles in there and shit. Yeah, it's not bad. Oh, it's like a Cuban sandwich.
Kind of. It's supposed to be grilled ham and cheese. You didn't enjoy your brunch? No. Where'd you go? I want to cook on some — we went to Guisados in Boyle Heights.
I want to cook on some future podcasts. You guys can cook anytime you want — there's a kitchen upstairs. No, but on the show. We're in the kitchen right now. Dude, you guys can cook anytime you want.
Wow, that's pretty good. How are you so skinny? Oh no, I have fat right here. No, you don't. You're super skinny, you're cut.
Is it because you skate all the time? Yeah, that's why. But you eat like shit, right? I eat like shit. I don't see you eating a healthy kale salad. I live right by In-N-Out Burger.

Whoa, that's dangerous. Do you like lentils and kale? No, I like meat. So what do you eat every day? Burgers. Every day, burgers? Oh, every other day. All right, so between the two of you, what's the best burger in LA?
Me? Us two? Yeah, the two fatties that eat all the time. You say Tommy's? Tommy's is the best? You think the best burger in LA is Tommy's? I like Hamburger Hamlet.
I don't know if it's still around. It's a constant, because people love burgers. I love burgers. It's probably my — you got me beat, go ahead. After pizza, it's like the most popular food.

Yeah, but every day, like, I'll lay in bed and be like, In-N-Out, something that's open, fast. But then it's like, I don't want In-N-Out, and I'm in LA, there's gotta be — you know, Father's Office, that's easy to say. But the best one, I think, is a place in Hawthorne. What's the—

Let me put it more specifically. What's the not-cool-guy — like Umami Burger and Father's Office, those are all, you know, hipster burgers. Where can you just get a burger that's awesome, that's not — you know, you're not Umami. You know what I'm saying?
